title: Assistant tasklet bundles — sketch & user stories
content:
Quick pitch (one line): lightweight, composable assistant "tasklets" that bundle intent-specific prompt scaffolding, cost tiers, and optional local heuristics so product teams can ship targeted micro-features without changing core routing or model surface.

Why this?
- We keep seeing customers want small, opinionated assistant behaviors (summarize + action, triage + escalate, short Q&A) but don’t want to manage separate endpoints or full rollout plans.
- Existing solutions: big model variants or coarse routing -> high cost or brittle UX. Tasklets = cheap, composable building blocks.

Problem statements / goals:
- Goal: enable product teams to define a named tasklet that encapsulates (prompt template, response budget, fallback policy, optional adapters like tools/format checks).
- Success: 3 internal teams adopt as experiment; median token cost per tasklet call < 40% of baseline; NPS from devs > 7 for ease of use.

User stories (rough prioritization):
1) As a product engineer, I can create a tasklet (name + template + budget) and call it from the same API route with ?tasklet=... so I don't need a dedicated model config or route. (high)
2) As a PM, I can attach a rollout policy and watch per-tasklet telemetry (tokens/calls/latency/error) in Console. (high)
3) As an SRE, I can configure a circuit-breaker per-tasklet that routes to a cheap fallback when errors/queue grow. (med)
4) As a UX designer, I can compose two tasklets client-side (short answer -> structured follow-up) and tag them to a session so the runtime preserves KV across steps. (med)
5) As a researcher, I can mark a tasklet as "regression-sensitive" to gate model variant changes. (low)

Core components (minimal MVP):
- Tasklet manifest (YAML/JSON) fields: id, display_name, prompt_template, max_tokens_budget, preferred_model_family, fallback_variant, tool_hooks (optional), regen_policy (single/iterative), redact_rules (optional).
- API surface: attach tasklet_id to generation request; server expands template, enforces token budget, applies prefix caching if session-bound.
- Console: quick create/edit, basic telemetry (cost per call, 90p latency, error rate), simple rollout selector.
- SDK: client helper to compose tasklets + optimistic local validations.

Implementation notes / rough infra impact:
- Prompt expansion: lightweight runtime stage before batching; must preserve batching semantics so tasklets don't break throughput. Could reuse existing prefix cache + continuous batching pipeline.
- Budget enforcement: runtime-level token accounting with pre-reservation (prevent overcommit) + graceful truncation/abort hooks. 
- Fallbacks: pluggable policies: model-fallback, lower-quality-shorter-response, canned static reply. Tie into smart routing layer.
- Telemetry: tag metrics with tasklet_id; add cost attribution to token-level billing pipes.

UX sketches (developer flows):
- Create tasklet in Console: name, paste prompt, set budget slider (Low/Med/High with token estimates). Toggle "session sticky" to retain KV cache for follow-ups. Save -> gets tasklet_id.
- Call: POST /v1/generate { input, session_id, tasklet: "purchase-summary-v1" } -> returns structured body + metadata (tasklet_used, tokens_billed).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Scope: Are tasklets just client-side conveniences + server-managed templates, or full first-class deployable artifacts (versioning, canary)? Start simple but design extensible.
- Security: user-provided templates might include variable substitutions — need strong sanitation & redaction. How to limit tool hooks?
- QoS interplay: if many tasklets prefer the same low-latency pool, could screw SLAs. Need per-tasklet throttling/priority.
- Billing model: per-call flat vs per-token attribution. Likely keep per-token but expose a consumer-friendly estimated cost.

Risks / mitigation:
- Proliferation of suboptimal templates -> noisy evaluations. Mitigate with presets + internal gallery + linting heuristics.
- Operational complexity (many tiny configs). Mitigate by namespacing tasklets to teams + retention policy + cleanup UI.

First experiment (2-week spike):
- Build prototype runtime expansion + budget guardrail (no console). Expose via SDK flag and track metrics for 2 internal features: (1) onboarding micro-tutorial summarizer, (2) billing assistant quick-recap.
- Measure: median tokens, 95p latency, developer time to integrate.

Notes / stray ideas (brain-dump):
- Tasklet gallery with samples (support copy-to-team) — lowers friction.
- "Tasklet chains" as a composition primitive (maps to multi-step workflows without new endpoints). Could be client composition first.
- Allow "soft budgets" where runtime suggests shorter response but can escalate on explicit user action.
- Provide a lint/checker that flags broad-language instructions (safety) and suggests structured output schema when possible.

Immediate next actions:
- Sync 30m with Miguel + Tess to align on telemetry fields and minimal manifest shape. (Ping Slack #prod-hosted-api)
- Create spike ticket (JIRA INF-2785) and a tiny GH PR to add tasklet_id passthrough in SDK.
- Draft Console mockup (low-fidelity) and add to Confluence page.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Sync infra constraints: batching, prefix cache implications (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Prototype budget guardrail in runtime (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Small SDK helper + example (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Create gallery seed templates (owner: Zara)

Random notes to self: keep initial manifest intentionally small. Resist adding tool-hooks until we understand security surface. End.
